questions.text: What best describes high-frequency ventilation and its primary goal?

answers.text: Small tidal volumes less than anatomic dead space at rapid frequencies, to provide gas exchange while limiting lung injury
Large tidal volumes at slow rates to maximize alveolar recruitment
Normal tidal volumes with very high PEEP to drive CO₂ removal
A non-invasive mode used to avoid intubation in neonates

questions.text: On HFOV, how is oxygenation primarily achieved?

answers.text: By maintaining a high lung resting volume (increased FRC) through a high mean airway pressure, similar to CPAP
By increasing the amplitude to deliver larger tidal volumes
By increasing the frequency to deliver more breaths per minute
By allowing passive exhalation through elastic recoil

questions.text: Which gas-transport mechanism describes gas mixing between lung regions that have different time constants, where fast-filling units empty into slow-filling units at end-inspiration?

answers.text: Pendelluft ventilation
Spike formation
Taylor dispersion
Molecular diffusion

questions.text: On HFOV, increasing the bias flow has what primary effect?

answers.text: It increases the MAP, which raises the PaO₂
It increases the amplitude, which lowers the PaCO₂
It increases the frequency, which lowers the tidal volume
It decreases the MAP and improves CO₂ clearance only

questions.text: On HFOV, how is the MAP titrated for lung recruitment, and how can it be set from conventional ventilation?

answers.text: Increase MAP until lung expansion reaches T8–T9; it can be set by adding +5 to the MAP currently required on conventional ventilation
Increase MAP until expansion reaches T4–T5; set it equal to the conventional MAP
Decrease MAP until the wiggle disappears; set it 5 below the conventional MAP
Set MAP to 33% of the PIP and do not adjust it

questions.text: On HFOV, frequency (Hz) has an inverse relationship with amplitude. To eliminate MORE CO₂, what should be done to the frequency?

answers.text: Decrease the frequency, allowing more time for pressure to reach the alveoli
Increase the frequency, delivering more breath cycles per minute
Leave the frequency unchanged and increase the I-time instead
Increase the frequency, which directly raises the amplitude

questions.text: Which statement about high-frequency jet ventilation (HFJV) is correct?

answers.text: It uses a nozzle/injector to create high-velocity jets with passive exhalation, and is used mostly for BPD, PIE, and air leak syndromes
It uses a piston to actively push and pull gas, and is the most common form of HFV
It requires active exhalation and a long I-time of about 0.33 seconds
It is used only in adult patients with ARDS

questions.text: On HFJV, which adjustment is the most important factor for decreasing the PaCO₂?

answers.text: Increasing the delta P by raising the PIP (and decreasing PEEP)
Increasing the PEEP to recruit more alveoli
Decreasing the rate below 240 BPM
Increasing the I-time toward 1 second

questions.text: On HFJV paired with conventional ventilation, oxygenation is improved by which of the following?

answers.text: Increasing PEEP, increasing the CV rate as a recruitment maneuver, and increasing I-time
Increasing the jet PIP and decreasing PEEP
Decreasing PEEP and increasing the jet rate
Lowering the MAP below 10 to reduce overdistension

questions.text: On HFJV, the servo pressure suddenly DECREASES. Which of the following could explain this change?

answers.text: Worsening compliance/resistance, an obstructed ETT, a tension pneumothorax, or a right mainstem intubation
Improving compliance or resistance
A leak around the ETT because the baby is growing
A tubing leak in the circuit
